newsitem.title: USA: Mubarak meets U.S. congressional leaders.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak meets U.S. congressional leaders.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak got a warm reception on Tuesday from U.S. congressional leaders as they discussed Middle East issues.
"We are always eager to visit with President Mubarak. He is a pillar of strength in the Middle East," House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich said before their meeting.
Gingrich and House International Relations Committee Chairman Ben Gilman, a New York Republican, also indicated their support for continued U.S. aid to Egypt, now about $2 billion a year.
"A prosperous, stable Egypt is absolutely essential," Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, said.
Mubarak invited Gingrich to visit Egypt and Gingrich said he hoped to do so soon. Gingrich leaves on March 23 for a one-week trip to Asia with stops in China, Hong Kong, South Korea and Japan.

Earlier, after lunch with members of the International Relations Committee, Mubarak said the U.S. veto on last Friday of a U.N. Security Council resolution condemning Israel for its plan to establish Jewish housing in east Jerusalem would not hurt U.S.-Egyptian relations.
"Egyptian-American relations are very strong. Nothing like this would shake it," Mubarak said.
Mubarak also met with Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott and Democratic Leader Tom Daschle and members of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.
"We have full support for the (peace) process," Mubarak said after the meeting with the committee.

Mubarak, who arrived in Washington on Saturday, met President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Monday. On Wednesday, he is scheduled to meet Vice President Al Gore, leaders of Jewish-American organisations and other members of Congress. Mubarak leaves on Thursday for Chicago.
